claim_verdicts.source: Chrome 153 headless via CDP, run by reviewer on scratch copy of examples/don-hang @ stage-0: www/index.html (no HTML/MDN docs root in versions.yaml; none under refs/)
claim_verdicts.evidence: Tree mirrors nesting: confirmed. But the lesson's own rule 'one node for each element and each piece of text' contradicts §4 'html sits at the top with two children, head and body'. Observed `document.documentElement.childNodes` = `HEAD,#text"\n",BODY` (3 child nodes, 2 element children). The body also holds 13 text nodes, 8 of them whitespace-only. The top of the tree is the document, with html as its top element.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: For www/index.html, the html element sits at the top with two child elements, head and body (plus a text node for the line break between them); body holds h1, p and ul; the ul holds three li, each holding an a.

claim_verdicts.source: Chrome 153 headless via CDP, reviewer scratch run (local server logging every request)
claim_verdicts.evidence: Script added a p after h1 on click: body became `H1 | P:Chào mừng! | P | UL`, 0 new requests; innerText (layout-based) reflected the change. But §4 'without the browser asking the server for anything' is too strong: a script that adds an img or a stylesheet link node makes the browser fetch that file. The outline says 'without downloading a new page'.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: When it changes the tree, what you see changes too, without loading a new page.

claim_verdicts.source: Chrome 153 headless via CDP, reviewer scratch run: navigate to view-source:http://127.0.0.1:8099/index.html after a script edit
claim_verdicts.evidence:
View-source showed `

Đơn Hàng

` and not the script-added 'Chào mừng!', so it does not show the live DOM: confirmed. But the server log recorded a new `GET /index.html` when view-source opened. Chrome asked for the file again (the server can answer from its copy or say 'unchanged'); it did not just show the stored text. So 'stays exactly as it arrived, and view page source shows that text' is too strong. DevTools UI not driven; CDP DOM.getDocument (its backend) returned the live tree.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: View page source shows the HTML file as the server sends it, not the tree. For a file that has not changed on the server, that is the same text the page was built from.

claim_verdicts.source: Chrome 153 headless via CDP, reviewer scratch run
claim_verdicts.evidence: After DOM.setNodeValue changed the h1 text to 'Xin chào', Page.reload produced server log `GET /index.html` and `document.querySelector('h1').innerText` = 'Đơn Hàng': the edited tree was discarded and a new one built from the HTML. Chrome only; no permitted doc root covers browsers.
`git show stage-0:www/index.html`: no

claim_verdicts.source: Chrome 153 headless via CDP, reviewer scratch run
claim_verdicts.evidence: Injected `h1.addEventListener('click', ...)` that runs `document.createElement('p')` then `h1.after(p)`; dispatched a real mouse press/release on the h1. Result: body children `H1:Đơn Hàng | P:Chào mừng! | P:Trang tĩnh... | UL`. The new p's parent is body, right after the heading, as §5 says. 0 new requests.

Chrome 153 headless --dump-dom on scratch fix.html (`
x

a

b`, no script)
claim_verdicts.evidence:
Mislabelled 'opinion': it is a behaviour claim, and as a general rule it is false. With no script at all, the DOM already differed from the source: `...` (tbody added) and `

a

b

` (closing tags added). It holds for a tidy file like www/index.html, which is the lesson's case.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Actually they match only for a tidy page, and only until something changes the DOM. The source is the text the server sent; the DOM is a tree in memory that JavaScript, or your developer tools, can change at any time.

issues.quote: When the two differ, the difference is exactly what the scripts have done.
issues.text:
Unlisted claim, and false as written. The lesson's own Try-it makes the DOM differ with no script at all (a DevTools edit). The browser also tidies HTML while building the tree: headless Chrome turned `` into `
` and closed `

a

b` with no script on the page.
issues.fix: Replace with: "On a tidy page like this one, when the two differ, the difference is what scripts, or your own edits in the developer tools, have done." Add it to claims (kind behavior).

issues.quote: Open the developer tools (F12 in most browsers) and choose the Elements or Inspector tab. ... View the page source (Ctrl+U)
issues.text: Unlisted claims: the F12 key, the tab names 'Elements'/'Inspector' and the Ctrl+U shortcut are specific facts that are not in `claims`. Ctrl+U is unhedged, and it is not the view-source shortcut on macOS. The prereq lesson did list its Ctrl+U claim, hedged as 'in most browsers'.

issues.text: Unlisted claim and an unsupported ranking ('the main thing'). No permitted source ranks what page scripts mostly do, and a script can run without changing the DOM. The same wording repeats in quiz q5 explanation.correct.
issues.fix: Replace with: "Actually JavaScript in a page can change the DOM: add, remove and edit nodes, and each change shows on screen at once." Apply the same change to q5 explanation.correct (en and vi).

issues.quote: `html` sits at the top with two children, `head` and `body`

issues.fix: Use claim 1 suggested_text: "two child elements, head and body".

issues.quote: without the browser asking the server for anything
issues.text: Too strong: adding an image or stylesheet node makes the browser fetch that file (claim 2). The outline says only 'without downloading a new page'. Summary line 3 says the same ('without a new request to the server').
issues.fix: §4: "without loading a new page". Summary line 3: "A change to the DOM shows on screen at once, without loading a new page."

issues.quote: It stays exactly as it arrived, and "view page source" shows that text, not the tree.
issues.text: In Chrome, opening view-source sent a new `GET /index.html` to the server (claim 3). What it shows is the file as the server sends it now. That matches the original only while the file is unchanged. The Try-it outcome is unaffected, because the lab file does not change.
